messages.content: Explain why the leaves of many trees change color in autumn. Answer in two to four sentences of plain prose.

message.content: Leaves change color in autumn because trees stop producing chlorophyll, the green pigment that captures sunlight for photosynthesis, as days grow shorter and temperatures drop. Once the chlorophyll fades, other pigments that were present in the leaves all along—yellow and orange carotenoids—become visible. Reds and purples come from anthocyanins, which many trees actively produce in the fall, possibly to protect the leaf as it transfers remaining nutrients back into the tree. Eventually the leaf's connection to the branch is sealed off, and it falls away.
